[[File:Starr 061105-1365 Citrus limon.jpg|thumb|Rough lemon]]
'''Rough lemon''' (''Citrus'' × ''jambhiri'' Lush.) is the fruit and the tree of a [[citrus hybrid]]. Like the [[Rangpur (fruit)|rangpur]], it is a cross between [[mandarin orange]] and [[citron]].

Rough lemon is a [[cold-hardy citrus]] and can grow into a large tree.

The rough lemon is mostly rind, making it less edible than other citrus. As a result, the rough lemon is mainly used for [[citrus rootstock]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=McPhee|first=John|title=Oranges|date=1967|publisher=Farrar, Straus and Giroux|isbn=978-0-374-51297-2|location=New York|language=English|oclc=934108}}</ref> however areas of South Africa and India do consume it and is the main lemon variety cultivated on [[Norfolk Island]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lemons! |url=https://www.norfolkisland.net/lemons/ |website=Discover Norfolk Island |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref> There are several [[cultivar]]s of rough lemon that can serve as a [[citrus rootstock]], including 'Florida',<ref>[http://www.citrusvariety.ucr.edu/citrus/floridarough.html Florida Rough lemon] at [[Citrus Variety Collection]] website.</ref> 'Schaub',<ref>[http://www.citrusvariety.ucr.edu/citrus/schaub.html Schaub Rough lemon] at [[Citrus Variety Collection]] website.</ref> and 'Vangassay' rough lemon.<ref>[http://www.citrusvariety.ucr.edu/citrus/rootstocks.html Citrus rootstocks] at [[Citrus Variety Collection]] website.</ref> The process for using the rough lemon as a citrus rootstock would start with mashing up the rough lemons. The mashed up rough lemons would then be put in a furrow, which is a long trench. This yellow mash would produce seedlings, which would end up growing into orange or grapefruit trees through [[shield budding]], also known as T budding.<ref name=":0" />
